previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a left total knee replacement due to severe degenerative joint disease. The surgery was performed on 2160-01-30 and proceeded without complications. Postoperatively, she developed acute posthemorrhagic anemia requiring four units of packed red blood cells over two days. Her renal function was closely monitored given her history of kidney transplant, and she was seen by nephrology. A urinary tract infection caused by E. coli, sensitive to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, was identified and treated. Pain was managed initially with a PCA pump, transitioning to oral acetaminophen and hydromorphone. She received Lovenox for DVT prophylaxis and was started on warfarin at discharge with instructions for INR monitoring. Physical therapy began on postoperative day one, and she achieved weight-bearing as tolerated. The wound was clean and healing without signs of infection. She was discharged home with home health services and detailed instructions on wound care, anticoagulation, and follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  History postop day 11 after a left total knee replacement with
bilateral lower extremity swelling and pain question DVT.

TECHNIQUE:  

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:

Gray scale and color Doppler ultrasound was performed of the right common
femoral, superficial femoral, popliteal, posterior tibial and peroneal veins. 
There is normal flow augmentation and compressibility.

Gray scale and color Doppler ultrasound was performed of the left common
femoral, superficial femoral vein and posterior tibial veins.  These
demonstrate normal flow augmentation and compressibility.  The left popliteal
vein and peroneal veins were unable to be visualized due to patient refusal
because of pain.

IMPRESSION:

1. No evidence of DVT in the right lower extremity.

2. No evidence of DVT in the left common femoral, superficial femoral or
posterior tibial veins.  The popliteal and peroneal veins were not visualized
due to patient discomfort.
